In brief: the claim is rejected as stated. The >85% electrical round-trip figure exceeds even the undiscounted Carnot ceiling (~64%, between 565°C and ambient) for a resistive-charge/Rankine-discharge system, and is also unmet by the best published "Carnot battery" (reversible heat-pump/heat-engine) architectures, which top out at 40–70%. At 5 MWh scale the cost claim also fails independently, because power-conversion equipment (turbine/heat exchangers) is fixed-cost-dominated and overwhelms a system this small, while lithium-ion capex scales linearly with kWh. Both failures trace to a single underlying error: the claim substitutes a thermal (heat-in/heat-out) efficiency and cost metric for the electrical-basis metrics its own comparison to a lithium-ion battery requires. Overall confidence: MEDIUM (the core impossibility finding is HIGH; the MEDIUM reflects unread supporting cost/efficiency citations on the cost and diagnostic chains).
